No license check exists anywhere in the code. Each phase ends when
its "real" list has been done against real systems, not when the code compiles.

## 0.1.0, the MVP

Built. The engine, durable executions, the Postgres queue and workers,
expressions, the Code step in its jail, the credential vault and OAuth2,
webhooks, schedules and MQTT, users with enforced MFA, OIDC, projects and RBAC,
audit, version history, the API, the editor, the connectors on the approved
list, workflow import, metrics and traces, the Helm chart and the Quadlet units.
Cut by `RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, not before.

## 0.2.0, identity and governance

Built, and shipped inside 1.0.0 with the new editor. SAML, LDAP and AD, SCIM,
custom roles, external secrets, log streaming, variables, folders, insights,
execution annotations, the S3 and Azure blob backends, and execution redaction
policies. Each one is tried against the real server it talks to, and each has a
screen in the editor.

## 0.3.0, environments and scale

Git source control and environments, protected instances, the multi-main HA
scheduler with trigger leases, the webhook role, concurrency and rate limit
controls, retention, backup and restore. It is done when I can kill the leader
main during a minute-level schedule and find no duplicate and no missed runs
over an hour.

## 0.4.0, connectors and people

The rest of the approved connector list, the published declarative connector
spec, a plugin SDK and index, and forms with human approval steps. Approvals
have to work from a phone, because the person approving a recipe change is
standing at the line, not sitting at a desk.

## 0.5.0, AI and MCP

LLM and agent steps, an MCP client and server, and a builder that uses your own
model. Bring your own key or run it local. There is no hosted service and there
won't be one.

## 1.0

Stability promises on the workflow file format and the API, an upgrade path
tested from every 0.x, and the docs.

## The new editor UI

Built, and in 1.0.0. The editor is rewritten in Astro with Svelte islands, built to
static assets and embedded in the Go binary the way the old one was, so it is the
same one-binary story with nothing new to run. It takes its colors, type and mark
from the HotLoop brand files, and follows the system's light or dark. Every screen
the old editor had is in it and does what it did (the canvas code came across
unchanged), the 0.2.0 features have screens, and a browser test drives each of
them against the real server in a real Chrome. Nothing about it changed the API,
the file format or the Go side.
